class_guidance: Choose the wordClass by what the thing IS. "places" is ONLY a location the child goes to (park, barn, store) — never a portable thing. Any living creature — pet, farm animal, sea creature, bug, or dinosaur — is "animal". A growing thing — tree, flower, seaweed, hay — is "plant". The rest of the outdoors — rock, mud, puddle, hill, sky, moon — is "nature".Anything edible is "food"; a beverage is "drinks". A person, role, or third-person pronoun (she, he, they) is "people"; I, me, my, you and your are "core".A day, month, season, holiday, clock word, or when-word (today, later) is "time".Use "object" ONLY as a last resort, for a man-made tool, vehicle, instrument, or piece of equipment (ladder, tractor, car, hose) that fits no more specific class — always prefer animal / plant / food / places / people first.

stages.I: at Brown's Stage I: single words, mean utterance length 1.0-2.0, no grammatical morphemes
stages.I/escalating: at Brown's Stage I: single words, mean utterance length 1.0-2.0, no grammatical morphemes
stages.II-III: at Brown's Stage II-III: mean utterance length 2.0-3.0, two- and three-word combinations, early grammatical morphemes only (present progressive -ing, the prepositions in and on, regular plural -s). Keep sentences short and concrete; do not use complex clauses
stages.II-III/escalating: at Brown's Stage II-III: mean utterance length 2.0-3.0, two- and three-word combinations, early grammatical morphemes only (present progressive -ing, the prepositions in and on, regular plural -s). They are insisting right now, so this sentence may be longer and more forceful than their usual level — keep the words simple, but do not shorten it back down
stages.IV+: at Brown's Stage IV or later: mean utterance length above 3.0, full simple sentences with embedding and coordination, including irregular past tense, possessives, articles and contractible copula
